newsitem.title: USA: Sears raises hostile bid, MaxServ accepts.
newsitem.headline: Sears raises hostile bid, MaxServ accepts.

text.p: MaxServ Inc. has agreed to be acquired by Sears, Roebuck & Co. after the retailer raised its hostile takeover bid to $7.75 a share or about $29 million, the companies said Monday.
Sears, which already owns 64.4 percent of MaxServ, said it extended its tender offer for the rest of the company's shares until March 14.

MaxServ provides information services for Sears customers and for the repair and servicing of appliances and electronics by Sears Home Services technicians. The Chicago-based retailer accounts for more than 90 percent of MaxServ's revenues.

The definitive agreement marks a turnaround for MaxServ, which had refused to discuss the offer unless Sears raised it to $8. Sears launched its first-ever hostile takeover on Feb. 4, and had said it would proceed with its original tender offer of $7 a share, or $27 million, because a negotiated transaction was unlikely.

But at a meeting on Sunday, the Special Committee of MaxServ's Board of Directors unanimously recommended approval of the new offer after deciding it was fair and in the best interests of the Austin, Texas-based company's stockholders.
The Special Committee has recommended that MaxServ shareholders tender their shares in the offer.
Sears' stock edged down 75 cents to $53.50 early on the New York stock Exchange. MaxServ edged up 31.25 cents to $7.625 on Nasdaq.
